knowledge_checks.title: Active Recall: 3.3.4
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. (1) What hypothesis does a chi-square GOF test? (2) How do expected frequencies arise? (3) What changes when parameters are unknown? (4) Name one reason contingency independence is not today's LO.
hints: Use CMP language from today's notes.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: GOF tests whether a sample is consistent with a stated distribution. Expected counts come from the hypothesised probabilities (and sample size). Unknown parameters are estimated and DF adjusted under CMP rules. Independence is tomorrow's LO.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Skipping the LO hinge or swallowing the next LO.

knowledge_checks.title: Checkpoint: 3.3.4
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. You test whether claim counts follow a Poisson distribution; λ is estimated from the same sample. (1) How are expected frequencies formed, and what happens to degrees of freedom when λ is estimated? (2) Refuse: 'A chi-square test of independence in a two-way table finishes GOF.'
knowledge_checks.body: Chi-square GOF with DF adjust if parameters estimated; refuse independence-as-GOF.
knowledge_checks.explanation: GOF compares observed to expected under a hypothesised distribution; estimating parameters reduces DF; independence is separate.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: (1) Expected frequencies = n × fitted Poisson probabilities using λ̂; DF = (number of bins − 1 − number of estimated parameters), so subtract 1 for λ̂. (2) Refuse: independence in a contingency table is a different LO from one-sample GOF to a named distribution.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Forgetting to reduce DF when parameters are estimated, or treating independence as GOF.
success_criteria: States expected frequencies from the fitted distribution and DF adjustment for estimated parameters.
Refuses equating GOF with two-way independence.
